title: Sampling to Monitor Fluorescence during Cell Lysis: Large-scale One-step Phage Infection of Cyanobacteria
author: Sarah Giuliani
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.fi2bkge

steps.title: Add ASW to fluorescence plate
steps.instruction: Dispense 180 µL artificial seawater (ASW) into each well of a 96‑well plate that is labeled as a fluorescence plate.

steps.title: Add unfiltered sample
steps.instruction: Pipette 20 µL of unfiltered sample into the ASW in each well to achieve a 10× dilution and mix well with the pipette.

steps.title: Process filtered samples
steps.instruction: Transfer 280 µL from each experiment bottle or sample tube into a 96‑well filter plate that is stacked onto a bottom 96‑well filtrate plate, then centrifuge the stacked plates at 1000 × g for 3 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 280 µL of each sample into the filter plate.
Centrifuge the filter plate and the underlying filtrate plate at 1000 × g for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Dilute filtrate sample
steps.instruction: From the filtrate plate, add 20 µL of filtrate into the corresponding ASW‑containing well to obtain a 10× dilution and mix well with the pipette.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Using the Tecan plate reader, run the “chla + phyco_onestep.prt” program: read chlorophyll a fluorescence at 680 nm (excitation 440 nm) and phycoerythrin fluorescence at 577 nm (excitation 544 nm).

steps.title: Plot fluorescence over time
steps.instruction: Plot fluorescence intensity versus time and use the curve to monitor the real‑time progression of the infection.
